scopeMarkdown:
Make gpux's one editable element, `EditableText` over `EditableTextState`, a rich text editor from the start. The owner decided this on 2026-10-17, choosing **one element whose capabilities grow in layers**, not separate plain and rich elements. A plain field is a rich field with no formatting and pays nothing for it. The epic covers:

- stored character formatting;
- font size, letter spacing and baseline shift per run in the shared text system;
- rows of different heights;
- paragraph formatting: alignment including justify, indents, spacing, line height and lists;
- inline objects;
- a rich (HTML) clipboard.

## Order and sibling epic

The owner also decided:
- **Two epics, run one after the other** in the `editable-text` worktree set (`~/.worktrees/editable-text/{Gpux,RayX,...}`, branch `feature/editable-text`). This epic runs first.
- **`gpux-platform-text-input` runs second.** It covers platform text input on iOS, Android and the web, touch editing, and an opt-in native field for credentials. It builds on this epic's selection geometry.
- **Rejected options:** native text fields as the default, and two separate elements.

## Starting point (origin/main 0eb1c1d; RayX origin/master 4ee806e9)

**Text system: one size per line.**
- `PlatformTextSystem::layout_line(text, font_size, runs)` takes one size per line (`crates/gpui/src/platform.rs` ~1527).
- `FontRun` is `{len, font_id}` and `ShapedRun` is `{font_id, glyphs}`. `LineLayout` has one `font_size`, `ascent` and `descent` (`crates/gpui/src/text_system/line_layout.rs`).
- `TextRun` has no size, spacing or shift.
- Letter spacing is one value per line, applied after shaping (`apply_letter_spacing_to_layout`).

**Text system: what already works per glyph.**
- Glyph rasterization keys (`RenderGlyphParams`) carry a size per glyph.
- Hit testing reads only x positions.
- `glyph.position.y` is already applied at paint.

**Text system: what assumes one size.**
- the platform shapers: CoreText on macOS and iOS, cosmic-text on Linux, Windows and Android, and the web's cosmic with canvas fallback;
- the four font-run merge loops in `text_system.rs`;
- line ascent and descent;
- four `layout.font_size` reads in `paint_line`.

**Editable text.**
- Formatting is revision-bound `EditableTextStyleRuns` of `HighlightStyle`, dropped on every edit (`invalidate_style_runs`). RayX's rich text editor diffs the text after each change and installs the runs again.
- `HighlightStyle` has no family, size or spacing, and `TextAlign` is only Left, Center and Right.
- History stores whole-text states (`history.rs`), and undo/redo replace the whole buffer.
- `TextLayoutMap` assumes one `line_height` everywhere: content height, hit testing, IME rectangles, the caret, selection quads, vertical and page movement, reveal, auto-scroll and the visible-row window.
- Multi-line center/right alignment is inconsistent: paint aligns each visual row, but caret, selection and hit testing use one offset from the widest row.

**Clipboard: what exists.**
- The clipboard holds text, image or file paths only (`ClipboardEntry`, not `#[non_exhaustive]`).
- RayX builds `ClipboardString` literals (`rayx_components_document/src/clipboard/mod.rs:526`).

**Clipboard: per-platform gaps.**
- The iOS clipboard reads a Rust string that is not NUL-terminated (`crates/gpui_mobile/src/ios/platform.rs:338`).
- Android's clipboard is an in-process stub.
- The workspace has no HTML dependency.

**RayX constraints.**
- RayX destructures `EditableTextEvent::Changed` irrefutably at eight sites. Adding a variant or a field breaks RayX.
- RayX matches `TextAlign` exhaustively (`charts/plot/label.rs:133`).
- RayX has one exhaustive `TextRun` literal (`charts/plot/label.rs:21-28`).

## Boundaries

**Policy stays with consumers.** gpux owns neutral editing: buffer, formatting storage, layout, paragraphs and lists, objects and the clipboard codec. Consumers keep their own:
- toolbars and keyboard shortcuts for formatting;
- documents and block structure;
- Markdown;
- collaboration;
- RayX's operation and undo-history services.

The text rule against gutters, folds, search and diagnostics in the layout files still holds. List markers are paragraph formatting, not editor gutters.

**Read-only rich text uses `EditableText` in `ReadOnly` mode.** `Text`/`StyledText` get per-run metrics through `TextRun`, but keep a uniform line height and single-font truncation (`LineWrapper`).

**Out of scope:**
- RayX adopting the new API. It is RayX's own follow-up epic; this epic only keeps RayX compiling.
- bidirectional text;
- tables;
- spell checking;
- collaborative attribute merging.

## Owner-dependent acceptance

None. Every criterion is proved by gpux's own lanes on the Mac (lanes A, B, C, D, E and F) and by the pull request's CI for Windows and Linux.

## Defaults recorded instead of open product decisions

**Lists:**
- The list indent step is 24 px per level.
- Bullets cycle •, ◦, ▪ by level.
- Numbers use 1., a., i. by level.

**Inline objects:** they are owner-rendered elements with a text and HTML fallback.

**Rich paste:** it is off by default, so plain fields stay plain.

**HTML codec:**
- The size cap is 4 MiB; anything larger is pasted as plain text.
- Headings `h1` to `h6` are pasted as bold paragraphs with sizes 2, 1.5, 1.17, 1, 0.83 and 0.67 times the base size.
constraintsMarkdown:
- **Plain path unchanged.** Text with no metrics, no stored formatting and no style runs keeps today's layouts byte for byte, takes the single-row splice path, and shapes no more than today.
- **Text rules** (`.agentx/memory/knowledge/gpui/text/rules.md`):
  - the prehashed line-layout key contract;
  - the shared font-run scratch pool;
  - decoration runs independent of shaping keys;
  - the policy-neutral boundary;
  - `set_view_id` for the backing entity;
  - manual scroll preserved.
- **Fast mode** frames stay equal to frames drawn from scratch. Any new field that changes shaping is part of the fast-mode text carry identity (`fast/text.rs` `shapes_as`).
- **Additive public API.** `EditableTextEvent`, `TextAlign`, `ClipboardString` and every editable-text item RayX uses keep their shape. New formatting events use a new type.
- **TextRun.** The new `TextRun` field is the one source-level change: struct literals need `..Default::default()`. RayX's one literal gets that paired change, which compiles before and after.
- **Provenance.** Zed closure files keep provenance discipline: record the gpux-local patch surface in the closure-update checklist.
- **Dependencies** come from crates.io only (no git or `[patch]`), and every crate still packages.
- **Tests.**
  - Each behavior gets its own new test group (`crates/gpui/tests/<group>.rs`, a platform crate's named test module, a conformance scene naming its lanes, a lane check, or a `tools/browser/specs` title prefix).
  - Sprint checks select exactly those groups.
  - Runtime proof runs in gpux's lanes through `gpux-testkit`. RayX checks prove only the consumer.
- **iOS and Metal runtime work** is closed only by lane F and lanes C/D on a Mac.
- **Diagnostics** go to the ignored `artifacts-temp/`.

requirements.title: Per-run font size, letter spacing and baseline shift in the text system
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: One line can mix font sizes, letter spacing and baseline shifts on every platform text system, and paint them correctly.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
**CoreText shapes each run at its own size**, on macOS (`MacTextSystem`) and iOS (`IosTextSystem`):
- Output glyph runs map back to input runs by string index. The read-back font is not usable, because the ligature-break trick shapes alternate runs at `size.next_up()`.
- Runs with the same font but different sizes are not merged.
- Fallback-font glyphs keep their run's size.
- Ascent and descent come from each run's sized font.

**Tests:**
- macOS: new test module `run_metrics` in `gpux-macos`.
- iOS: lane F check `text-run-metrics-ios` lays out a mixed-size line through `WindowTextSystem` and asserts per-run sizes, increasing x, and an ascent at least the larger run's.

requirements.title: Stored character formatting
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: `EditableTextState` owns character formatting that moves with edits, undoes with them and renders through the text system.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
**Where inserted text gets its attributes.** Text inserted at a caret takes the attributes of the character before it. At a paragraph start it takes the character after it; in an empty paragraph, the paragraph's last attributes.

**Explicit typing attributes.** `set_typing_attributes` (for example, bold toggled with no selection) applies to the next insertion. It is discarded when the caret moves or focus changes.

**IME composition** takes the typing attributes for its whole life and keeps them on commit.

**Links and tags** are never extended by typing at their end: their end is exclusive.

New group `editable_text_typing_attributes.rs`.

**Undo and redo restore formatting.**
- History entries keep spans, paragraph formats and objects with the text, shared rather than copied per keystroke.
- An attribute change over a range is its own undo step, never merged into typing.
- Typing still coalesces under typing attributes.
- Undoing an edit restores the exact spans.

**Revisions.**
- A formatting-only change does not bump the buffer revision. It bumps a separate format revision.
- `EditableTextEvent` is unchanged. A new event type reports formatting-only changes.

New group `editable_text_format_history.rs`.

**Rendering stored attributes.**
- Family, weight, style, size, letter spacing and baseline shift become shaping runs.
- Color, background, underline and strikethrough become paint runs.
- The owner's revision-bound `EditableTextStyleRuns` (syntax highlighting, search hits) still apply on top for the paint fields they set.

**Plain fields pay nothing.** A field with no stored attributes and no style runs takes today's path, including the single-row splice, with identical layout and shaping counts (`TextLayoutCacheStats`).

**Incremental shaping.** Typing in formatted text reshapes only the edited row; unchanged rows are cache hits.

**Tests:**
- group `editable_text_attribute_layout.rs`;
- new scene `editable-rich-attributes` (lanes A, B and C): bold, italic, size, color, background, superscript and subscript in one field, with probes.

requirements.title: Rows of different heights
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: Editable layout and every geometry consumer handle visual rows with their own heights, baselines and alignment.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
**One alignment offset per visual row.** Caret, selection, hit testing and IME geometry use each visual row's own alignment offset: the one paint uses.

**The bug this fixes:** today, center- or right-aligned multi-line fields offset geometry by the widest row.

**Test:** new group `editable_text_row_alignment.rs`, proven to fail against the old code. It uses a centered paragraph whose two rows differ in width.

requirements.title: Paragraph formatting
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: Paragraphs carry alignment, indents, spacing, line height and list items, and move with edits.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
**Alignment values:** left, center, right and justify, as a new paragraph-level enum; `TextAlign` is unchanged. Unset means the element's `text_align`.

**How justify works:**
- It widens inter-word spaces so every row ends at the trailing indent.
- The paragraph's last row is left-aligned, and so is any row with one word.
- Caret, selection, hit testing and IME geometry follow the justified positions.

New group `editable_text_paragraph_alignment.rs`.

**Indents:**
- The first row starts at leading indent plus first-line indent. A negative first-line indent is a hanging indent, clamped at the field's edge.
- Other rows start at the leading indent.
- Every row wraps at the field width minus the trailing indent.

**Spacing, line height and letter spacing:**
- Spacing before and after adds vertical space outside the rows.
- The multiplier scales the paragraph's rows.
- The paragraph's default letter spacing applies to runs that set none.

**Tests:**
- group `editable_text_paragraph_spacing.rs`;
- new scene `editable-paragraphs` (lanes A, B and C): centered, right-aligned, justified, indented, hanging-indent and spaced paragraphs, with probes.

requirements.title: Lists
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: Paragraphs can be bullet, numbered, checkbox or custom-marker list items with nesting, painted markers and the expected editing.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
**List item settings.** A paragraph's list item has:
- a kind: bullet, numbered (with a start number), checkbox (with a checked state), or a custom marker string;
- a nesting level.

**Layout:**
- The leading indent grows by a per-level step: 24 px by default, settable on the state.
- The marker paints right-aligned in the space before the item's first row, on its baseline, with the size and color of the item's first character.

**Markers:**
- Bullets cycle •, ◦, ▪ by level.
- Numbered items format as 1., a., i. by level.
- **Numbering:** a numbered item counts the consecutive numbered items at its level. Deeper items in between do not break the count; a non-list paragraph, or a different kind at that level, restarts it.
- A checkbox item paints a box showing its state. A click or tap on the box toggles it, as an undoable format change.

**Markers are not text.** Caret, selection, IME `text_for_range`, `text()` and plain-text copy never include them.

**Tests:**
- group `editable_text_lists.rs`;
- new scene `editable-lists` (lanes A, B and C).

**List editing defaults.** Each is also a public state method, so an owner's own key bindings can call it, and owners can switch them off per state. Each is one undo step:
- **Enter in a non-empty item** splits it into two items.
- **Enter in an empty item** ends the list: the paragraph loses its list format instead of getting a line break.
- **Backspace at the start of an item** removes its list format before any join.
- **Tab and Shift-Tab in an item** raise and lower its level. Shift-Tab at level 0 removes the list format.
- **Tab outside a list** propagates, as today.

New group `editable_text_list_editing.rs`.

requirements.title: Inline objects
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: Owners embed elements inline in text: chips, mentions, images.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
**Insertion.** An owner inserts an inline object at a range. The buffer gets one U+FFFC character carrying an object attribute:
- the owner key;
- width, height and baseline offset;
- a text fallback;
- an optional trusted HTML fallback.

**Layout:**
- The object reserves exactly its width, replacing the placeholder glyph's advance.
- Its height and baseline offset count in the row's height.
- It is never split across rows, and a row may break before or after it.

**Editing.** Caret, selection, deletion, undo and attribute changes treat it as one character.

**Text and export:**
- IME `text_for_range` and `text()` contain U+FFFC.
- Plain-text copy writes each object's text fallback.
- HTML copy writes its HTML fallback, or else its escaped text fallback. This needs the HTML codec, so it is proved with it: an object with and without an HTML fallback in `editable_text_html.rs` (CLIP-2) and `editable_text_rich_clipboard.rs` (CLIP-3).
- `AttributedText` carries objects.

New group `editable_text_inline_objects.rs`.

**Painting.** The element paints each visible object by asking an owner-supplied renderer for the element of its key. It places that element in the object's box, as a child clipped by the field.

**Pointer events** over an object reach that element's listeners first. They fall back to text selection when it does not handle them.

**No renderer.** An object without a renderer still reserves its space but paints nothing.

**Tests:**
- group `editable_text_inline_render.rs`;
- new scene `editable-inline-objects` (lanes A, B and C): a colored chip and an image-sized box inside text. A click on the chip is handled by the chip.

requirements.title: Rich clipboard
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: Formatted text copies and pastes as HTML on every platform, through a safe HTML codec.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
**Copy and cut.** `EditableText` writes plain text plus HTML when the selection holds any stored formatting, paragraph format, list or object. Otherwise it writes plain text only, as today.

**Paste:**
- With rich paste accepted, the HTML's formatting is inserted. It is a per-state switch, off by default, so plain fields stay plain.
- Otherwise plain text is inserted.
- Every paste is its own undo step, never merged into typing. This includes platform-driven pastes through the input handler, which gets an item-aware paste whose default keeps today's behavior.
- Single-line fields flatten paragraphs.

New group `editable_text_rich_clipboard.rs`.

**Objects.** HTML copy of a selection holding inline objects writes each object's HTML fallback, or its escaped text fallback (OBJ-1's HTML export), tested in this group.

requirements.title: Compatibility and documentation
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: Additions stay additive for gpux's consumers, and the rich model is documented.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
**Documentation:**
- **New `docs/editable-text.md`** describes the editing model:
  - character formatting, paragraphs, lists and inline objects;
  - typing attributes, history, the rich clipboard and its HTML subset;
  - the policy-neutral boundary.
- **Closure-update checklist** (`.claude/skills/gpux/references/update-from-zed-gpui-closure.md`): add the rule to preserve per-run metrics through `TextRun`, `FontRun`, `ShapedRun`, every platform text system, the merge loops, cache keys, the fast-mode text carry and paint.

Verified by review.
